subject: Private runtime compatibility & shared-services constraints - RFI
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@medicor.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medicor.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Private runtime compatibility and shared services constraints

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Medicor is evaluating a private deployment for sensitive PHI workloads and we need a clear picture of runtime compatibility and any constraints your private package places on our environment. High-level asks:

- Can your private runtime run completely offline in a VPC with no outbound internet? Any components that require egress?
- KMS/HSM: support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) and integration options.
- Operator access model: can we restrict operator accounts to a jump-host + bastion and deny vendor interactive shell access?
- Upgrades/patching for airgapped customers — process, signed bundles, rollback options.
- Shared services: does your package require LDAP/AD, internal DNS, NTP, or access to our internal package mirrors?
- SBOM and third-party dependency disclosure for attestation.

Please route technical responses to me and CC your engineering lead. We'd also like an SBOM snapshot and any sample airgap upgrade playbook.

Regards,
Emily Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Medicor Health

(Attachment: procurement-nda.pdf referenced below)
From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karl_sales_ops@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Private runtime compatibility and shared services constraints

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (privacy/compliance). We prepared a concise RFI packet and a short SBOM coverage extract attached; see attached: private-runtime-answers.pdf and sbom-coverage.csv.

Top-line answers here to help your review quickly:

- Offline/VPC: Yes — our Private distribution supports completely offline installs. Core control plane components do not require outbound connections when deployed with the airgap bundle. Optional telemetry/analytics connectors require explicit config to ship out; defaults are disabled.
- Egress: No mandatory egress. We do recommend time-limited outbound for license verification during onboarding (can be skipped if you validate license offline).
- KMS/HSM: BYOK supported via standard interfaces (KMS via REST + KMS plugins; HSM via PKCS#11). Details in the attachment and Marissa will follow up with diagram.
- Operator access: We support role-based access with operator account separation and an audit-only vendor account. Interactive vendor shells are off by default; privileged operations use signed operation-tokens and require customer approval.
- Upgrades/patching: Airgap bundles are signed with our vendor key. We provide an upgrade playbook; upgrades are reversible (snapshot/rollback) if taken with recommended pre-flight checks.
- Shared services: LDAP/AD is optional — we ship an LDAP proxy and token-based alternatives. DNS/NTP can be configured to use internal infra. Package mirror support is available; we can seed images from a local registry.
- SBOM: Attached CSV shows third-party coverage; full SBOM can be provided under an NDA (we saw your attachment).

Next step: Marissa will provide deeper integration diagrams and the airgap upgrade playbook. If helpful, propose a 60-min technical workshop next week to walk through your operator constraints and network diagrams.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

(Attachments referenced: private-runtime-answers.pdf, sbom-coverage.csv)
From: security@medicor.com <security@medicor.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFI follow-up: shared services and observability egress

Rafael — couple of technical clarifications from our security/infra team after reviewing the initial packet: 

1) Shared services: we run central AD via LDAP, internal DNS, internal package mirrors and a restricted NTP tier. Will your LDAP proxy support AD group-to-role mapping and AD signed certs?
2) Observability: you mentioned optional telemetry. Where do runtime logs/metrics live by default for a private install? Can we ensure logs never leave our VPC?
3) Third-party binaries: are any runtime components closed-source/third-party binaries that require network license checks?
4) Upgrade timing: for production clusters we require scheduled windows and a canary node upgrade model with automatic rollback on probe failures. Do your playbooks support this?

Thanks — Emily (cc'd) asked me to gather these specifics before scheduling a workshop.
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: security@medicor.com <security@medicor.com>, emily.chen@medicor.com
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: shared services and observability egress

Hi Medicor team — Marissa here from Solutions. Answers inline below.

1) LDAP / AD integration
- We provide an LDAP proxy that performs group-to-role mappings. Customers can upload mapping rules and bind profiles.
- We accept AD-signed certificates for LDAPS; certificate chains can be provided at install time.

2) Observability / logs
- Default for Private installs: logs and metrics are written to local storage and your customer-managed observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK) by default.
- Outbound telemetry is disabled unless explicitly configured. We offer an optional shipping agent that can forward aggregated telemetry to a customer-managed collector inside the VPC or to a configured internal syslog endpoint.
- We support retention and encryption-at-rest policies that you control.

3) Third-party binaries / license checks
- The runtime is built from open-source components except for a small, Redwood-signed binary that performs kernel binding optimizations (we supply source-level disclosure under NDA).
- No mandatory network license checks for runtime operation; license verification is optional during initial onboarding and can be performed offline with a signed token exchange.

4) Upgrade / canary model
- Airgap upgrade bundles are signed. Our upgrade playbook supports canary upgrades at node-level and automated pre/post-upgrade probes. If probes fail, the playbook triggers an automatic rollback to the previous snapshot. We include pre-flight checks and recommended SLAs for upgrade windows.

Other notes:
- KMS/HSM integration: we support KMS via customer-managed endpoints and HSM via PKCS#11 modules. Key rotation is supported and logged to your audit store.
- Operator access: we recommend a jump-host model and provide RBAC primitives and audit hooks. Vendor operator accounts are audit-only unless you opt-in for elevated support sessions.

Attachments: airgap-upgrade-playbook.md, kms-integration-diagram.png

If this covers your asks, Rafael can book a 60-minute engineer-to-engineer workshop (we can do a network diagram walkthrough and discuss your mirror/proxy topology).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
